1 Corinthians 4:2
Identify broker, sales agent, client, other party, and intermediary status before applying the rule.
Disclosure, IABS & Minimum Services▾
Representation must be clear and minimum duties cannot be ignored.
Client

A client is the party represented by the broker under the brokerage relationship.

Minimum services

Texas law requires a representing broker to perform specified baseline duties such as presenting offers and answering client questions.

Material information to client

A broker representing a client must inform the client of material information about the property or transaction received by the broker, subject to law.

Honesty and fairness to all parties

Texas brokers must treat all parties to the transaction honestly and fairly even while advocating for a client.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Texas Intermediary Practice▾
One broker can work between both sides only inside the statutory framework.
Intermediary

Texas intermediary is the statutory method for a broker to act between parties to the same transaction with required written consent and restrictions.

Intermediary without appointments

Without appointments, the intermediary broker remains impartial and cannot give partisan opinions or advice that favor one party.

Intermediary with appointments

With the required consent, an intermediary broker may appoint different associated license holders to communicate with and advise each party. Appointments require enough associated license holders to appoint one to each party. If the company has only the broker, or the broker and only one agent or associated broker, intermediary may still be possible but without appointments.

Intermediary confidentiality

An intermediary generally cannot disclose a seller's willingness to take less, a buyer's willingness to pay more, or protected confidential information without authorization or legal requirement.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Broker-Sales Agent Relationships & Supervision▾
The broker remains responsible for the brokerage system.
Sponsoring broker responsibility

A broker bears regulatory responsibility for brokerage activity conducted through sponsored sales agents within Texas law and rules.

Written policies and procedures

Texas sponsoring brokers must maintain current written policies and procedures covering specified supervision topics.

Compensation through broker

Sponsored sales-agent compensation for brokerage activity remains subject to the sponsoring broker's control and Texas payment rules.

Broker succession

Texas law provides a transition framework when a licensed entity loses its designated broker, with a limited period to restore compliant broker designation.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Unlicensed Assistants▾
Administrative help cannot turn into unlicensed brokerage.
Clerical/administrative activity

An unlicensed assistant may perform genuine administrative tasks that do not involve brokerage judgment, negotiation, or prospect representation.

Showing property

Showing property or independently providing access to prospects generally requires a real-estate license in Texas.

Prospecting / solicitation

Unlicensed assistants may not prospect for brokerage business in ways that require a license, such as soliciting listings.

Handling rents/security deposits

Texas limits unlicensed assistants' authority to accept rents or security deposits in brokerage property-management activity.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
2026 Texas Buyer Agreements & Non-Representation Showings▾
Texas changed the written-agreement rules effective January 1, 2026.
Written agreement before residential-buyer brokerage activity

For a prospective buyer of residential real property, a Texas license holder generally must enter into the written agreement required by TRELA before showing residential property to that buyer, or, if no property will be shown, before presenting an offer on the buyer's behalf. The agreement may establish representation or, when the statutory conditions are satisfied, a limited non-representation showing arrangement.

Showing without representation

A license holder using the statutory non-representation path may show property without becoming the buyer's agent only within strict limits. The license holder may provide specified factual information such as size, price, and terms, but may not provide opinions or advice to the buyer/tenant or perform other brokerage services for that party under the non-representation showing arrangement.

Written-agreement disclosures

The 2026 framework requires the written agreement to address the services to be provided, termination, exclusivity or non-exclusivity as applicable, representation status, compensation, and conspicuous disclosure that broker compensation is not set by law and is negotiable.

Who is outside the residential-buyer requirement?

The 2026 written-agreement requirement in TRELA §1101.563 applies to prospective buyers of residential real property. It does not apply to commercial purchasers or to residential or commercial tenants, although other agency and disclosure rules may still apply.

Showing-only non-representation limits

A non-representation showing agreement must be non-exclusive and may not run longer than 14 days. The license holder may provide limited factual information such as size, price, and terms, but may not give opinions or advice or perform other brokerage services for that buyer or tenant under the showing-only arrangement.

Open-house distinction

A host from the listing brokerage does not need a buyer agreement merely for a walk-in prospective buyer at that listing-brokerage open house, but must disclose representation of the owner. A host outside the listing brokerage who does not represent the seller must provide IABS and enter the required written agreement before showing the property to the prospective residential buyer.

🎯
Exam trap: IABS, a representation agreement, and a non-representation showing agreement are not interchangeable. Identify the relationship first, then ask what written agreement and notice are required before the activity described.

Know when TREC forms apply, what license holders may complete, and when legal drafting belongs with an attorney.
Promulgated Contracts, Forms & Addenda▾
Use the right form and stay inside the licensee's drafting authority.
TREC promulgated form

A promulgated form is adopted by TREC for license-holder use in transactions to which the form applies, subject to recognized exceptions.

Form-use exception

Texas recognizes limited exceptions to required promulgated-form use, including certain attorney-prepared or government-required forms.

Addendum

An addendum supplements the main contract with authorized standardized terms or disclosures for a specific issue.

Special Provisions boundary

Special Provisions is for permitted factual/business information and is not a license to draft complex custom legal rights or remedies.

🎯

One-to-Four Family Contract Logic▾
Read the form by function instead of memorizing isolated paragraph numbers.
Effective date

The effective date is the contract-formation date from which many performance deadlines are measured under the form.

Earnest money / option fee delivery

The current Texas contract form sets delivery requirements for earnest money and option fee and includes timing rules for weekends or holidays.

Title policy / survey

Texas contract forms allocate title insurance, title commitment, survey, objection, and cure responsibilities.

Property condition / access

Texas contracts address buyer access, inspections, utilities, property-condition elections, and seller disclosure when applicable.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Statute of Frauds & Enforceability▾
A valid deal can still have an enforceability problem.
Statute of Frauds

Texas law generally requires real-estate sale contracts and certain brokerage agreements to be in writing and signed to be enforceable.

Electronic signature

Electronic signatures can satisfy contract signature requirements when valid under applicable electronic-transactions law.

Definite property description

An enforceable real-estate contract must identify the property with legally sufficient certainty.

Written compensation agreement

Broker compensation rights depend on satisfying applicable written-agreement requirements.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Seller Disclosure Requirements▾
Seller disclosure and buyer inspection are separate systems.
Seller's Disclosure Notice

Texas Property Code requires many residential sellers to provide a statutory property-condition disclosure notice, subject to defined exemptions.

Disclosure timing

The timing of delivery can affect the buyer's statutory or contractual termination rights.

Disclosure exemptions

Texas law identifies certain transfers in which the standard Seller's Disclosure Notice is not required.

As-is provision

An as-is agreement allocates property-condition risk within legal limits but does not authorize fraud or intentional concealment.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.

Use category recognition first, then apply the Texas-specific rule.
Community Property & Homestead▾
Separate marital-property character, creditor protection, and tax exemption.
Community property

Texas generally treats property acquired during marriage as community property unless it qualifies as separate property under Texas law.

Separate property

Separate property can include property owned before marriage and qualifying gifts or inheritances received by one spouse.

Homestead protection

Texas homestead law protects a qualifying residence from many creditor claims subject to constitutional and statutory exceptions. For conveyance questions, a married homestead generally requires the joinder of both spouses even if record title appears in only one spouse's name, subject to statutory exceptions.

Homestead tax exemption

The homestead tax exemption reduces taxable value for qualifying property-tax purposes and is distinct from creditor protection.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Wills, Estates, Recording & Equitable Interest▾
Track how interests pass and how notice protects them.
Testate succession

A person dies testate when property passes under a valid will, subject to probate and Texas estate law.

Intestate succession

Intestate succession applies when no valid will controls the property and Texas descent-and-distribution rules determine heirs.

Recording statute

Recording real-property instruments gives public notice and helps determine priority among competing claims under Texas law.

Equitable interest

An equitable interest is a beneficial or enforceable interest recognized in equity even though legal title may be held by another.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Landlord-Tenant, Foreclosure & Short Sales▾
Distinguish lease remedies from mortgage remedies.
Security deposit accounting

Texas landlord-tenant law regulates handling, deductions, and accounting for residential security deposits.

Landlord security devices

Texas residential law imposes duties concerning specified locks, keyless deadbolts, smoke alarms, and security devices under applicable conditions.

Nonjudicial foreclosure

Texas commonly uses nonjudicial foreclosure for deeds of trust when contractual and statutory power-of-sale requirements are satisfied, though important exceptions exist.

Short sale

A short sale is a lender-approved sale in which proceeds are insufficient to fully pay the secured debt.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Mechanic's Liens, VLB & HOAs▾
Texas-specific liens, veteran programs, and private community governance.
Mechanic's and materialman's lien

Texas law provides lien rights to qualifying persons furnishing labor or materials for improvements, subject to strict procedural requirements.

Texas Veterans Land Board (VLB)

The VLB offers qualifying Texas veterans state-supported land, housing, and home-improvement financing programs under current program rules.

Homeowners association (HOA)

An HOA enforces recorded private covenants and community rules subject to Texas statutes and governing documents.

HOA lien / foreclosure

Qualifying HOA assessments can create liens and enforcement rights subject to Texas notice, procedure, and owner protections.

🎯
Read the facts first, identify the governing rule, and then eliminate answers that confuse a related but different concept.
Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act (DTPA)▾
Consumer protection belongs in Special Topics.
DTPA purpose

The Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act is a consumer-protection law aimed at false, misleading, deceptive, and other prohibited practices in consumer transactions. Real-estate facts can raise both TREC discipline issues and separate DTPA/private-liability issues.

Misrepresentation and consumer reliance

When a fact pattern describes a false factual representation, concealment, or deceptive conduct that affects a consumer transaction, do not stop at “ethics.” Ask whether the conduct may also create statutory consumer-protection exposure.

Remedies are separate from license discipline

TREC discipline is an administrative remedy. A consumer claim under the DTPA is a separate legal path and can involve damages when statutory elements are established. One set of facts can create more than one kind of consequence.

🎯
Exam trap: “TREC can discipline the license holder” and “the consumer may have a DTPA claim” can both be true. Read what remedy or legal framework the question is asking about.

CRESS Exam Psychology

Understand Your Mind Before You Test It.

Passing is not only about knowing real estate. It is also about retrieving what you know while your body is under pressure. This section trains calm, focus, pacing, working memory, endurance, and decision control.

CRESS
01Calm the bodyLower the physical noise before demanding clear thinking.
02Protect working memoryOne question at a time. Do not mentally carry the last question forward.
03Control paceFast is not the goal. Clear and steady is the goal.
04Build staminaTrain your brain to stay seated, focused, and accurate for the full testing window.
Mindset Scripture
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.”
2 Timothy 1:7
A sound mind is not a rushed mind. Your job on test day is not to prove how fast you can answer. Your job is to remain clear enough to recognize the rule you already studied.
What Test Anxiety Does to Your Thinking▾
Stress can use up the same mental space you need for the question.

Working memory is the small amount of information your mind can actively hold while reasoning. Under pressure, thoughts such as “I am running out of time,” “I cannot fail,” or “What if I do not remember this?” compete with the facts in the question. The result can feel like suddenly forgetting material you actually know.

The CRESS interpretation

A blank moment is not automatic proof that you do not know the material. First reduce the pressure signal, then reread the facts and retrieve the rule.

Test Moment

You read a familiar agency question and your mind goes empty. Instead of rereading it five times in panic, stop looking at the choices, exhale slowly, identify the relationship first, then return to the answer choices.

🎯
Rule: Do not answer the fear. Answer the question.
The 60-Second Reset Before You Begin▾
Your first task is physiological control.
1. FeetPlace both feet on the floor. Let your shoulders drop.
2. ExhaleUse a longer, comfortable exhale for several breaths. Do not force a giant breath.
3. VisionLook at one fixed point and let your eyes settle before reading.
4. Statement“I only have to solve the question in front of me.”
5. StartRead the stem slowly before looking for speed.
💡
Do not wait until panic is high. Use the reset at the beginning, after a difficult cluster, and anytime you notice yourself speeding up.
Stop Rushing: The C.L.E.A.R. Question Method▾
Use the same decision sequence on every hard question.
CCalm

One slow exhale. Release the urgency.

LLocate

What is the question actually asking for?

EEliminate

Remove answers that are legally wrong, off-topic, absolute, or from the wrong concept.

AApply

Apply the governing rule to the facts, not to what you wish the facts said.

RRespond

Choose the best answer, flag only when necessary, and move forward without reopening the decision emotionally.

🎯
Do not change an answer merely because another choice suddenly “sounds smarter.” Change it only when you can name the rule or fact you originally missed.
Build Sitting-Still and Focus Endurance▾
Exam stamina is trainable.

If most study sessions are short, interrupted, or phone-heavy, the testing room can feel unusually uncomfortable. Train the exact behavior you need: sitting, reading, deciding, and continuing without novelty.

Level 125 minutesNo phone. One section. Accuracy first.
Level 245 minutesMixed questions. One planned reset only.
Level 375 minutesLong-form practice with no entertainment breaks.
Level 4Full simulation80-question National or 40-question Texas attempt under exam-like conditions.
The purpose

You are teaching your nervous system that sitting with uncertainty is not an emergency. A difficult question can exist without forcing you to rush, quit, check your phone, or mentally abandon the exam.

When You Blank, Second-Guess, or See Two Good Answers▾
Use a recovery protocol instead of an emotional reaction.
BlankingHide the choices mentally. Name the topic. Recall one rule. Then reread.
Two answersAsk which answer addresses the exact legal issue in the stem, not merely a related concept.
Second-guessingRequire new evidence before changing your answer.
Hard questionMake your best reasoned choice, flag it if needed, and protect the rest of the exam.
Decision Control

If a question asks what a license holder should do first, an answer describing something that might happen later can be legally true and still be the wrong answer. Read the task word: first, best, most likely, required, prohibited, before, after.

Exam-Day Pacing Without Racing the Clock▾
The clock is information, not a threat.

Use broad checkpoints rather than checking the timer after every question. The goal is a steady average pace with enough room to review flagged items. Do not spend several minutes trying to force certainty out of one question while sacrificing easier questions later.

Two-pass discipline

Pass 1: answer what you can reason through and flag only genuinely uncertain items. Pass 2: return to flagged items with the remaining time. Avoid reopening unflagged answers without a specific reason.

💡
Your score comes from total correct answers, not from winning a battle with the hardest question on the screen.
How to Review a Practice Exam▾
Every missed question needs a diagnosis.
Knowledge miss

I did not know or remember the rule.

Reading miss

I knew the rule but missed a word such as NOT, EXCEPT, FIRST, or BEST.

Application miss

I knew the definition but could not apply it to the facts.

Rushing miss

I answered before finishing the stem or choices.

Second-guess miss

I changed a correct answer without new evidence.

Math/process miss

I used the wrong formula, unit, percentage, or sequence.

🎯
Do not merely record the correct letter. Write the reason you missed it. That turns practice into training.

CRESS Mastery Strategy

First prove understanding. Then train under pressure.

01Understanding Builder

More direct rule recognition and application. Use these to confirm that you actually understand the content before chasing speed.

02Rigorous Simulation

More application and analysis, tighter distractors, longer fact patterns, and choices that may all sound reasonable until you identify the controlling rule.

03Comprehensive Final

Blueprint-weighted mixed difficulty. Treat it like test day: steady pace, limited second-guessing, and a full review of every miss.

🎯
Texas exam alignment: State simulations follow the current Pearson VUE Sales Agent State Law outline: Commission Duties & Powers, Licensing, Standards of Conduct, Agency/Brokerage, Contracts, and Special Topics. CRESS questions are original practice questions; they are not copied from the state exam.

CRESS full simulations use the scored blueprint counts: 80 National/General and 40 Texas State. Pearson VUE's actual Sales Agent examination also includes 5 unscored National pretest items and 10 unscored Texas pretest items. Those pretest items are not identified, so answer every question.
